blocks.text: Sulfur usually forms single bonds with other sulfur atoms instead of double bonds due to poor overlapping of the orbitals. As a result, it forms larger molecules and structures through a process called catenation. S₈ is a crown-like molecule, as shown in Figure 12.7.

blocks.alt: Eight S atoms joined by single bonds in a closed, puckered ring drawn as a crown: an upper zigzag row of five S atoms and a lower row of three S atoms, the two ends of the upper row joined down to the lower row.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.7: Cyclo-octasulfur, (S8) crown molecule (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.7).
